FIRST PROTOTYPE
6 private cards

Per character, dealt from one shared deck. Start with 3 characters; test tiered abilities at totals 15, 21 and 24. See the full evaluation for rarity-based alternatives.

SHARED-HAND BRANCH
8–10 cards

For the card-count model, compare upgrade frequency with remaining party actions. The rarity-only model also considers H=12.

POWER MODEL TO TEST FIRST
More cards → more power

Pay for stronger effects with a larger subset. Compare rank-based patterns separately. Extra cards cost more but are not always rarer.

The original targets converge

With eight cards and any 2–5 played, 15, 21 and 31 are each available in over 92% of hands. Higher totals do not automatically mean rarer abilities.

A high Decision Density means several physical card choices. It does not mean those choices can all be played: they may reuse the same cards.

Power from cards spent

Exact At H=8, five-card 21 occurs in 29.73% of hands; at H=10 it is 56.39%. These are paid upgrades. Any total above 40 forces five cards, so it cannot offer a cheaper version.

Card-count columns overlap; a hand can offer more than one size. The final column is the five-card option conditional on any activation being possible. Joint highest-tier distributions and party spending analysis.

Critical opportunities

Any 2–5 cards. Rank probabilities are simulated; numeric-value probabilities are exact. “Possible” is proven by the complete pattern catalogue. Conditional rate means a critical option exists given an ability is available, not that the player chooses it.

Private hands

Keep scarcity local to the character. H=6 gives 15/21 about 81% availability per character, 31 about 58%, 37 about 32%, and 39 about 24%.

  • Ownership supports character-specific abilities.
  • A 4-character party holds 24 cards, not 6.
  • Another character having the target does not help a unique class ability without trading.

One shared hand

Creates card-allocation decisions. In an illustrative {15,21,31} menu, a shared H=12 hand funds all 3 characters about 89% of the time, all 4 about 57%, and all 5 about 4%.

  • Cards spent by one actor are unavailable to another.
  • Equal-budget pooling of private hands makes many single abilities nearly automatic.
  • Use fallback actions or explicitly test refill and action-budget rules.

Critical asymmetry matters

Rank runs unlock 37, 39, 44, 47 and 49. Numeric matching treats all sixteen ten-valued cards as interchangeable: 20/30/40 become much more critical-friendly, and every successful 50 automatically crits.
